clauses.title: Native owner installation
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The owner can inspect the operating description before dependency installation; setup preserves this edition’s native owner and selected bindings. Local setup exits with no app running; dev prints a private entry address that enters as the real local owner through the rer dev v2 boundary, preserving native sessions, roles and passwords. Reset is explicitly confirmed and local; export/import preserve supported native data with documented exclusions. Deployment dry-run makes zero outbound requests and explicitly reports that fact. A separately and explicitly started read-only provider preflight uses the owner's scoped Cloudflare token with owner consent to read the account's Workers subdomain and the Worker's settings and secret names (three GETs for an existing Worker); it sends no mail and changes no resources. Dry-run and preflight are independent steps, neither a mock of the other. The delivered runtime requires no original checkout or PHP service. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md). **Acceptance.** 1. Use a clean checkout through rer describe/check, locked installation, setup, dev, verify, reset and export/import; preserve owner/data/settings and refuse unconfirmed destructive work. 2. For deployment dry-run, assert zero outbound requests and an explicit no-outbound report without provider credentials. 3. As a separate acceptance point, explicitly start the read-only provider preflight with owner consent and the owner's scoped token; assert only the three expected Cloudflare GETs for an existing Worker, no mail and no mutations, and refuse missing credentials or consent. 4. Prove the runtime works independently of the original checkout; separately qualify remote provisioning.

clauses.title: Retained native password identity
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Preserve native password sign-in, first-owner setup, the accepted owner experience and prior account/workspace data with the maintained Base command mechanisms. Retain this edition's authentication and native owner setup. A second factor for these native accounts is required by IDENTITY-003; it adds to native passwords and never replaces them. Supersedes `BASE-ACCESS-001` for native password identity under RL-1. **Acceptance.** 1. Complete native password setup, login, recovery and workspace re-entry, then upgrade with prior owner credentials and data intact; configured providers must not replace native identity.

clauses.title: Scoped authority
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Owner setup, registration, login/recovery, project switching, membership and widget admission establish native identity. Provider configuration never substitutes for user authority. The public widget key and origin are not a secret: visitor, registration and project-creation requests are bounded by D1-backed limits (the documented admission limits) and refused with HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`. A stored widget session serves only the visitor identity the host page supplies now (its identifier, else its email in any letter case, else anonymous); an unsigned sign-in carries the browser's anonymous conversation over, unverified; and `h2h('shutdown')` ends the browser's widget sessions. **Acceptance.** 1. Through native session and widget routes, deny cross-tenant, blocked/deleted and revoked access; prove public admission returns 429 with Retry-After when limited and provider configuration conveys no actor authority. 2. In one real browser against the emitted Worker and the built widget, prove that account switches, sign-out, emulated pages and signed identities never send, read or render another visitor's session or conversation; that sign-in carries the anonymous conversation over and a returning signed-in visitor gets its own back; and that `h2h('shutdown')` removes the widget and forgets the browser's sessions in every state.

clauses.title: A useful first workspace
clauses.text: **Requirement.** First-run setup is one screen: the owner's email, a password, the website and, only where the server requires one, the private setup token. Missing names and colors are derived and every derived value can be changed. A completed installation leads the owner to a workspace that is already set up, whose Setup page lists only what cannot be done for them (an AI service key, the widget on their website and, with a hosted email provider, a verified sending domain), leads with the widget, lets the owner skip any of them for now, and shows everything else under "What we've set". Every workspace created by first-owner setup, signed-in workspace creation or email-verified registration, and never a demo workspace, is provisioned in one step: a starter assistant as its default visitor assistant, a reply-by-email mailbox when the installation holds the installation’s inbound-email credential, and mail sent from the installation sender until the workspace's own domain is verified. The starter assistant’s visitor replies carry external, and its internal preparation standard; the company’s policy decides each call once a provider key and complete policy exist, within that policy’s AI spending limits; with no key no assistant is assigned to a new conversation, it stays with the team and the AI page and Setup say a key is missing. The first-run Create workspace action may send one welcome email to the owner; an uncertain send is never replayed. Ordinary workspace creation leads with the widget snippet; Advanced retains the server secret and verification examples. Empty inboxes offer installation, a link to Setup and a demo. Workspace headers follow workspace switching. Visitor headers retain the operator's display name. **Acceptance.** 1. Run fresh first-owner setup and signed-in workspace creation to Setup and an installable widget; inspect derived editable name/color, starter assistant, mailbox/sender, skip/Advanced controls and mobile headers. 2. With no model key a new visitor stays with the team; with a configured provider exercise the capped starter. 3. A workers.dev hostname must not become a business name.

clauses.title: Rer dev mail
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Trusted local development configuration uses the rer dev v2 development transport: it validates and suppresses visitor and teammate mail, reports `development`, stores no messages and exposes no mail viewer. It sends no external email. The local owner enters automatically through the dev boundary; native password identity, ordinary hosted email-link confirmation and prior stored data are retained. Production has no local dev surface. Missing credentials or failed remote delivery never select a local substitute. **Acceptance.** 1. Enter through rer dev v2; send visitor and teammate mail and prove development suppression without storage, viewer or external send; refuse forged and production dev entry and never substitute suppression for a failed hosted provider.

clauses.title: Durable transcript
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Customer, operator, generation, import and administrative writers preserve stable message/command identity, revision/frontier, attachment ownership and final-reply admission atomically. Competing or repeated writes cannot admit two incompatible final replies. Owner/admin contact erasure removes message content while keeping identity, revision and frontier, so erased transcripts stay coherent. **Acceptance.** 1. Race visitor, operator, model and import writers through conversation routes with duplicate and lost responses; admit only compatible final replies. 2. Erase a contact through the owner door and verify coherent identity/revision/frontier with content removed.

clauses.title: Live delivery and recovery
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Persist before broadcast; reconnect/outbox replay and socket authorization recover committed messages after reload, disconnection or process wake. Provisional AI deltas never become durable final answers until guarded admission succeeds. **Acceptance.** 1. Disconnect/reconnect widget and operator sockets after persisted writes, restart the runtime and recover the same committed messages/attachments; unauthorized replay is denied and superseded AI deltas never become final replies.

clauses.title: Existing editable experience
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Reuse the original React dashboard, transcripts/drafts/suggestions, settings and Shadow DOM widget; preserve useful desktop/mobile flows, attachment display, collector/privacy controls and errors. Native routing and transport use the configured application origin. **Acceptance.** 1. Use the native dashboard and separately installed widget at 1440 and 390 pixels with realistic conversations, attachments, drafts, errors and workspace switching; retain the approved desktop/mobile navigation and configured-origin transport.

clauses.title: Reviewed history import
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Current workspace owner/admin reviewers privately upload, inspect per-kind plans, source-located omissions, rejections, conflicts and publication changes, then explicitly apply bounded, resumable imports of conversations, contacts, tags, saved replies and articles. Preserve source identities, timestamps, private notes and publication state; reject unsupported meaning rather than inventing it. Recheck current role and workspace authority for apply, resume and whole-import undo. Retain immutable source custody and conflict-safe reversal journals. Imports and undo send no mail, widget messages, model requests, assignment or connection notifications; imports are excluded from Reports. Native tag controls enforce workspace scope. RL-2 requires exact business-state repeat/undo equality, including contacts, conversations, messages, private notes, tags, source links and every other imported business table. Only platform counters/sequences, audit history and import journals are excluded. Synthetic 1,000-conversation datasets for Zendesk and Help Scout qualify this local flow. **Acceptance.** 1. Through Move in, exercise all five kinds, source custody, per-row omissions/rejections/conflicts, current-role denials, inert apply/resume/repeat/undo and exact business-state equality for synthetic 1,000-conversation Zendesk and Help Scout datasets; counters/sequences, audit and journals are the only named exclusions.

clauses.title: Resolution feedback and provenance
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Current original visitor sessions may rate a closed resolution with thumbs up/down and an optional comment up to 1,000 characters. Changes retain history; reopened cycles cannot receive the previous resolution's rating. Operators retain access to each past resolution's latest feedback after reopening; visitor eligibility and report denominators remain tied to the current cycle. Erasure removes rating comments. Confirmed operator-sent drafts establish assisted outcomes, otherwise confirmed human replies establish human outcomes. AI requires a complete visible answer history without a person handoff; missing evidence remains unknown. Status, assignment and cancellation transitions recheck current authority atomically. **Acceptance.** 1. Close, rate, rerate, reopen and close again via widget/operator routes; prevent previous-session/cycle feedback, retain old-cycle operator visibility, redact erased comments and verify human/assisted/AI/unknown attribution from actual visible answers.

clauses.title: Workspace calendar reports
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Native conversations created in the workspace IANA calendar range with at least one persisted message form the cohort; Move in and legacy imports are excluded. First visitor-to-visible-answer response and creation-to-first known-resolution durations use median and nearest-rank p90. Each conversation contributes its latest closed cycle once to outcome and satisfaction rates. Reopened conversations leave those denominators. Aggregate queries return bounded data; CSV streams every matching conversation with formula-safe cells. Empty widget conversations stay durable but are excluded from Reports and its analytics CSVs. A separate step-up guarded JSON export includes all workspace conversations, messages, private notes and attachment names across dates and imports; attachment bytes stay in the portable backup. **Acceptance.** 1. Compare Reports and formula-safe CSV to hand-calculated response/resolution median and p90, latest-cycle outcome and satisfaction cohorts across DST and tenants, including more than 10,000 rows and excluded imports/reopened cycles.

clauses.title: Workspace integrations
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Owner/admin tokens have explicit scopes, optional expiry, one-time display, hashed storage and durable audit. Bearer-only API calls have no CORS, per-token limits and native guarded writes. Contact erasure fences API identity restoration and pending event payloads. Native events commit tenant-bound webhook and Slack intents; historical import apply and undo do not emit them. Slack projects bounded native visitor text through Base escaping. The owner-authorized ordinary HTTPS exception retains redirect refusal, bounded requests/responses and literal-destination checks instead of DNS pinning (RL-3). See [the full transport exception](docs/contract/support-protocols.md). **Acceptance.** 1. Issue, use, expire and revoke each scoped show-once token; exercise native API operations, erasure fences, signed events and Slack escaping. 2. Refuse redirects/unsafe literal destinations and over-limit traffic; preserve timeout, streamed bounds, uncertain 500 without replay and bounded 429 behavior under the recorded HTTPS override.

clauses.title: Observed owner setup
clauses.text: **Requirement.** An owner sees the durable, project-scoped eight-step list on the Setup page; the genuinely empty inbox shows one next action and a link to it, and loads none of it. A step is confirmed only by an observation, never by a saved configuration, an installer default or a preset, so a workspace with nothing observed yet is zero of its applicable steps. The system runs its own checks: while an owner is signed in the page asks the server to observe, bounded by freshness windows. These checks are non-generative metadata, domain and DNS reads and never send mail. They distinguish saved configuration from observed sender DNS, authenticated model metadata, an inbound receipt, effective runtime ceilings, allowed origin and an authenticated widget ping; whether an article is published is not one of them (that step stays among the eight ids but is hidden and never counted). Mail to the owner is confirmed by a used emailed sign-in link, or by the provider's reported outcome for the welcome or test email; local development mail is suppressed and never confirms delivery, and provider acceptance or queueing is pending. Reading Setup performs no provider work and writes nothing. Only an explicit owner action (Create workspace, or Send me a test) may send mail, to that owner's mailbox, with durable identity; ambiguous work is never replayed. Missing provider permissions and unsupported status APIs remain unavailable. Configuration changes invalidate observations; model and DNS validation expire after 15 minutes and every observation shows its time. The owner can skip an owner-only step (the widget, the AI service, the sending domain) for now, and undo it. A skip is stored on the server for the workspace, can be made by an owner or admin only, makes no provider request, and moves the step out of Needs you and out of the confirmed count and its total; a skipped step is never shown as confirmed. An observation always wins: a skipped step that is later observed is confirmed and counted, and a rejected provider key stays under Needs you whether or not it was skipped. Provider keys and their fingerprints never enter API responses or browser storage. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md). **Acceptance.** 1. Read Setup without side effects, observe fresh/expired/rejected configuration and explicit provider outcomes, skip/undo owner steps and reload. 2. A skip or preset never counts as confirmation; local suppression never proves delivery; keys/fingerprints remain server-only and uncertain explicit test/welcome mail is never replayed.

clauses.title: Configured model execution
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Retain Ensemble model selection, context/tools, streamed events, normalization, raw per-round provider usage, attribution, bounded suggestions and reply lifecycle. Missing providers fail explicitly when AI is asked for, and a default assistant whose provider has no key is simply not assigned to new conversations; uncertain provider attempts remain uncertain and are not replayed automatically. Usage is diagnostic/provider accounting data, not an active payment, balance or debit system. Visitor-caused model work carries the classes of its eventual action, and the company’s policy sets its project and installation AI spending limits; a skipped reply is recorded as terminal and never replayed. Each workspace's AI reply mode is auto (the default), draft or off: in draft AI writes only drafts its team sends themselves, in off AI generates nothing, no AI-authored message reaches a customer in draft or off by any path (a local computer agent's reply becomes a draft its operator sends themselves, and a visitor whose assistant will not answer is handled as one without an assistant), in draft or off a conversation whose visitor has written since its assistant last answered is listed in the team's normal views as one without an assistant, and switching back to auto releases nothing queued, written or due during that time. **Acceptance.** 1. Request configured suggestions/replies through native routes; inspect normalized streaming events, per-round usage, context/tool and budget bounds, explicit missing-provider errors and durable daily-cap skips; crash/ambiguous attempts must not automatically replay.

clauses.title: Published knowledge
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Dataset ingestion/crawl, retained corpus, lexical/selected semantic retrieval, citations and article/category authoring maintain project scope and publication state. A failed refresh cannot replace the last usable published corpus. Public pages exclude drafts/deleted projects and preserve original canonical article/search routes. **Acceptance.** 1. Publish and search articles/categories through authoring and public help-center doors; deny draft/deleted/cross-project access, verify citations and canonical links and retain the last usable published corpus after a failed refresh.

clauses.title: Attributed customer context
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Profiles, monitoring, insights and context packets preserve evidence attribution, source bounds, consent and project ownership. Provider output must satisfy the selected schemas before becoming usable customer context. **Acceptance.** 1. Generate/read profile, monitoring, insight and context packets through native routes; reject ungrounded/schema-invalid or cross-project content, preserve attributed evidence and respect consent/source bounds.

clauses.title: Explicit local authority
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Pairing, devices/grants, revocation, tool context and work/result states preserve investigation, resolve and advance-authorized resolve-and-reply distinctions. Revocation withdraws authority and never asserts that a local process stopped: started work becomes terminal with an unconfirmed outcome, and only the device may report cancellation. Local processes remain in the optional connector, never an implicit Worker capability. Agent calls use the company’s policy for their computed classes; any approval or review in this journey is under the held company policy. **Acceptance.** 1. Under the held company policy, pair the packaged connector, investigate, separately authorize a child fix, obtain a distinct read-only observation and use human Send with exact-request replay. 2. Under the held company policy, refuse stale/revoked/offline/unverified/uncertain work and distinguish resolve from advance-authorized resolve-and-reply; revocation cannot assert process cancellation.

clauses.title: Durable evaluation
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Training and evaluation preserve run/case state, model/budget selection, raw provider usage and cancellation/recovery. Synthetic data admission is explicitly local/test-only. Historical pending attempts require reconciliation; a fixture pass is not live-provider quality acceptance. **Acceptance.** 1. Create, run, cancel and recover persisted evaluations through training routes with model/budget selection and raw usage; reconcile historical pending/uncertain attempts and keep synthetic admission local/test-only.

clauses.title: Honest external effects
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Email/inbound mail, GitHub, branding and knowledge imports use configured native adapters, tenant-scoped credentials, durable identity and ambiguous-outcome handling. Website previews use a separate origin, scoped expiring grants and public-network restrictions. Machine-generated inbound mail is a loop-suppression input, not a customer request or notification trigger; its classification is recorded before admission and survives recovery and redelivery. The `email:` message local-id prefix is reserved for inbound claims and refused by the message API. Shopify, Stripe and CRM support actions are required by COMMERCE-001, BILLING-001 and CRM-001. HappyToHelp never holds funds or becomes a payment processor; historical imported balances remain custody records, not executable authority. **Acceptance.** 1. Use configured email, inbound mail, GitHub and knowledge-import public doors; test idempotency, machine-generated-mail suppression, separate-origin preview grants and network denial. 2. An operator reply emails the visitor even with an online/unverified widget; a visitor address matching the reply sender is intentionally excluded and the message status explains that cause. 3. Test accepted, failed and uncertain outcomes without invented delivery; business-action evidence is also required by COMMERCE-001, BILLING-001 and CRM-001.

clauses.title: Homepage hero and two support moments
clauses.text: The public homepage leads with “Knows what your customer needs before they do.” A checkout offer and a prepared reply to a Spanish-store support question share a hand-drawn aqua composition. Numbered captions explain help before a customer asks and an agent-prepared fix awaiting human Send. The wide layout places the headline beside the drawing; the phone layout stacks them. Reduced motion shows the completed drawing. The exact publisher contract remains authoritative.

clauses.title: Free product promise
clauses.text: **Requirement.** “Not just better. Free.” (100% free and open source, free as in code and free as in cost, MIT licensed, “No seats. No plans. No fees.”, each promise after a line icon in a pale aqua circle, with the MIT license drawn as an ink card over a wordless code editor, “free of charge” and the rights highlighted in aqua); **Acceptance.** 1. The Free section retains the no-seats, no-plans, no-fees promise, MIT license, aqua icon circles and ink license over a wordless editor. 2. The page makes no price, hosting, provider or unrelated-service promotion.

clauses.title: Support desk, move-in invitation and closing
clauses.text: **Requirement.** “The rest of your support desk” (chat widget, shared inbox, help center, suggested replies, as frameless ink cards numbered on filled aqua discs); “Try it beside what you have” (install, bring the help center from Zendesk, Intercom or Freshdesk, add the chat widget, on filled aqua discs, beside the finished import in its window); “Ready when you are.”, a big closing headline with an aqua pen line drawn under it; and the footer, signed with the header's lockup. **Acceptance.** 1. The desk presents chat widget, shared inbox, help center and suggested replies as frameless numbered ink cards. 2. The move-in section offers install, help-center import from Zendesk, Intercom or Freshdesk and widget installation beside the finished import drawing. 3. The closing headline and footer retain the aqua line and header lockup, in the published section order.

clauses.title: Public brand, links and motion
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The public brand preserves the exact paper, ink, aqua drawings, licensed hand-drawn mark, real text and repository-derived links in [the retained public design](docs/contract/public-design.md). Local fonts and metric-matched fallback prevent text movement. Each below-hero moment appears once without layout shift; reduced motion leaves its final state complete. The approved drawing, frame, color, underline, spark, animation-property and timing details remain binding in that specification (RL-10). **Acceptance.** 1. The retained public design uses off-white paper, near-black ink, pill controls, pale aqua blobs and only the specified aqua accents and mark sparks. 2. Text and drawing labels remain real DOM content; repository-derived links resolve to the selected repository. 3. Self-hosted Outfit and its metric-matched fallback preserve layout; the hand-drawn wordmark retains its accessible name and licensed letter shapes. 4. Every below-hero moment plays once within 1.8 seconds without layout shift; reduced motion leaves every final drawing and stroke complete. 5. Keyboard navigation and the homepage’s permitted-width layouts preserve the approved experience.

clauses.title: Documentation and public knowledge routes
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Documentation renders the listed Markdown pages at build time, in the homepage's paper, ink and Outfit, with section navigation, page contents and GitHub links for everything unpublished; an unknown page gets the branded not-found page. Every build renders the current files, and an unlisted Markdown file fails verification. Dynamic published help centers retain project scope, canonical links, search and draft/deleted denial. The customer widget remains available through owner-configured installation; broader marketing routes, pricing, legal, referrer, waitlist and public auto-widget behavior are outside this edition. **Acceptance.** 1. Every listed Markdown page renders from current source with the retained section navigation, page contents, source links, responsive layout and detailed documentation specification. 2. Unlisted Markdown and broken links fail verification; an unknown page receives the branded not-found page. 3. Published help-center routes retain canonical links and search while denying drafts and deleted workspaces.

clauses.title: Prior-data custody
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Explicit legacy artifacts preserve IDs, exact historical financial values, transcripts, object hashes, publication and permissions through resumable guarded D1/R2 import. Historical financial SQL, imported rows and reconciliation holds remain immutable archive custody; they never become active payments, balances or provider work. The one exception is an explicit owner/admin contact erasure: it takes precedence over archive custody for that contact's personal data and redacts the imported rows and their verbatim archive copies (row digests are kept, so replaying the bundle does not restore them), leaving a opaque erasure audit tombstone. Old credentials do not become trusted native authority. Until legacy is retired, delta exports since a recorded watermark sweep what legacy took after the export into the seed, applying a legacy change only where the seed has not changed the row, never writing project rows, never updating identity rows and never restoring an erased contact's data. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md). **Acceptance.** 1. Import representative legacy IDs, permissions, exact historical financial values and media hashes through local D1/R2; resume safely and refuse conflicts without external work. 2. Erase an imported contact and prove archive redaction plus tombstone/digest fencing prevents restoration of erased personal data. 3. Export a delta since the full export's watermark and import it into the imported seed: new and seed-unchanged rows apply, a conversation gains its new messages in order, project rows stay the seed's after legacy retires the project, a row changed in both places is listed as a conflict without content, an erased contact's new data is not restored, no work starts, a rerun changes nothing and the delta check passes. The sweep after legacy's retire, imported with the retire's marker, imports a marked customer's new messages and conversations as live rows and lists no marked customer as a conflict, while a customer deleted at another time stays archive-only; a delta resolution offers no survey, and another writer's conversation fence stays.

clauses.title: Author-owned capability graph
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The edition selects maintained source with inspect/check/lock/release commands. Shared capabilities include substantial implementation, migrations and meaningful tests; a second consumer preserves its own policy. Release selects the licensed tree and retains asset provenance/licensing obligations. Original work is preserved. **Acceptance.** 1. Run inspect/lock/check and offline Base-copy verification on staged intentional source, exercise origin/drift/mode refusals and release only the selected licensed tree without credentials or private fixtures; source custody alone is not product acceptance.
