clauses.title: Signed HTTP monitoring
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Public hosted HTTP(S) and keyword checks run in the Cloudflare Worker; private checks use the separately scoped Node runner. They retain the exact immutable assertion bundle and bounded transport evidence, and require authenticated claims and signed results; the control plane must reject contradictory completion. Hosted Worker checks leave through Cloudflare's shared egress and have no dedicated source address; published allowlistable probe addresses and probe identification are PROBE-002's. See [Integrity and authority](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#integrity-and-authority) and [Network and credentials](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance.** 1. Create an HTTP(S) and keyword monitor through the owner API, run scheduled hosted and signed runner work against a controlled HTTPS service, fail its status/text, recover it and inspect the immutable assertions and transport evidence.

clauses.title: Immutable scheduled evidence
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Definitions, scheduled slots and every retry attempt retain revision, policy, fixed selected probes, runner identity, timings, status, assertions and error category; retries never erase failures, and observation/state/outbox commit atomically. See [Evidence and state](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#evidence-and-state) and [Integrity and authority](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance.** 1. Through signed claim/result routes submit failure, retry, late and duplicate attempts, restart, and read history; each attempt and its revision remains identifiable and observation/state/outbox either all commit or none do.

clauses.title: Fixed coverage and incident hysteresis
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Missing or expired passing coverage is Unknown, partial failure stays visible, independent-vantage agreement and scheduled confirmation determine Failing, and complete fresh scheduled passing evidence plus recovery threshold is required for recovery; manual checks and maintenance never rewrite observations or scheduled policy. See [Evidence and state](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#evidence-and-state). **Acceptance.** 1. Run two assigned network vantages through partial, missing, stale, failing and recovering slots; inspect Unknown/Degraded/Failing and thresholds. 2. A manual pass, absent probe or maintenance expiry cannot fabricate recovery.

clauses.title: Server-side scoped authority
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Runner claim, result and heartbeat doors accept only scoped runner authority; missing configuration fails closed; browser mutations enforce configured origin; expired or foreign attempts cannot alter current evidence, and duplicate attempt identities cannot overwrite it; a signature identifies a key holder rather than proving truthful observation. See [Integrity and authority](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance.** 1. Open private documents and call native/framework APIs while signed out, revoked, cross-origin or using a foreign/expired runner signature; require refusal with no product writes, then succeed with the authorized session or scoped runner.

clauses.title: Pinned bounded destination execution
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Every public DNS answer and redirect hop is validated fail closed; private-runner numeric sockets preserve Host and TLS identity, hosted checks use Cloudflare’s public Internet fetch transport, unsafe/mixed addresses and HTTPS downgrade are rejected, cross-origin redirects strip request authority, and synthetic grants and protected origin-bound local credential files retain their separate custody limits. The PROBE-002 identification header follows these credential rules and is stripped on cross-origin redirects. See [Network and credentials](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance.** 1. Exercise real controlled HTTP/TLS endpoints with mixed DNS, rebinding, hostname mismatch, redirects, downgrade, forbidden addresses, credentials and execution bounds; inspect requests and prove rejected destinations receive no connection or authority. **Bounded qualification.** `tests/tls-auth.mjs` mounts `tests/network-rebinding-support.mjs` proveNetworkRebinding once, with `tests/network-rebinding-routing.mjs` controlling only the authorized DNS and socket edge: an owner-created public HTTPS monitor and the production signed runner retain scheduled history through pre-connection A-to-B rebinding, next-due forbidden-B refusal and restored-A execution across a persistent Worker restart. Independent destination listeners and an ordered edge journal check numeric A, original Host and SNI, verified TLS, zero forbidden-B connections and requests, a passing canary, and Unknown with Incomplete fixed coverage and no fabricated incident or recovery on refusal. This qualifies only that rebinding cell; broader redirect re-resolution, address families, credential combinations, execution bounds, hosted transport and managed locations remain unproved, and the clause remains partial.

clauses.title: Revision-scoped receipt evaluation
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Hashed owner-issued tokens and, in the header form, increasing sequences protect server-time receipts, ingress cannot advance health, and scheduled signed completion must match its exact installation-local claim snapshot; stale, future, paused, foreign-revision or imported receipts cannot establish Healthy. These rules bind every receipt form of the buyer-facing job heartbeat in HEARTBEAT-002 and HEARTBEAT-003. See [Network and credentials](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance.** 1. Issue and rotate a heartbeat token through the owner door, send increasing receipts, miss one, and evaluate scheduled signed snapshots; replay, old tokens, imported or foreign-revision receipts cannot change current health.

clauses.title: Inactive validated restore
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Bounded versioned archives require integrity and semantic validation before transactional restore into empty product data, preserve historical evidence, erasure receipts and the permanent anonymized action audit, create paused current revisions, interrupt leases and quarantine alerts; installation-local sessions, keys, grants, request credential values, heartbeat authority, contact, webhook and Slack URLs, and signing keys are excluded; destination definitions and retained notification histories are portable, and imported evidence cannot establish current health or replay events. The source erasure journal fences copies made before a later erasure when that journal accompanies the restore. A local CLI receiving checkout must run setup first to establish its owner and settings. Supersedes `BASE-DATA-001` for installation authority and endpoint credentials only: the owner accepted this archive policy on 2026-10-13 (RL-1), as an intentional replacement, not BASE-DATA-001 equivalence. See [Portability and retention](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#portability-and-retention) and [Integrity and authority](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance.** 1. Export a populated installation including TCP, DNS, TLS and domain monitors, establish a different receiving owner, import into empty product data, then export/read history and repeat the restore. 2. Each protocol’s settings and immutable revisions/slots survive; definitions are paused, leases interrupted, delivery quarantined, secrets/authority absent, history retained and later erasure journals enforced; corrupt/nonempty imports write nothing.

clauses.title: Reviewed definition files and inactive imports
clauses.text: Versioned monitor definition files and saved monitor pages are previewed without writes and validated with the editor’s rules. Applying a matching plan creates paused monitors or new revisions that preserve enablement, maintenance and runner assignments. Files carry no request secrets or installation authority and cannot enable monitors, issue heartbeat tokens or change notification destinations. Batch undo preserves history and reports revision conflicts. Imported history never becomes current evidence. No real third-party export or hosted import has been measured.

clauses.title: Explicit storage custody
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Beyond BASE-DATA-002, short-lived login-attempt counters are cleaned up, and legacy development sign-in records stay until operator erasure or local reset. Expired or confirmed alert-drill links lose their capability material while drill history stays; retired destination secrets are scrubbed only after owner rotation/deletion and in-flight sends finish; a proven-unsent integration-attempt reservation can be removed while its delivery history remains. Expired discovery jobs retain their expired status. Raw target response bodies and probe-request secrets are not retained in observations; the only target content kept is EVIDENCE-002's bounded, redacted, access-controlled failure snapshot, stored apart from observations under owner-set retention, carried in archives and erased with its monitor or on owner request. Webhook and Slack endpoint URLs and signing keys remain installation-local, available email addresses travel as destination definitions, and retention changes must never silently improve the fixed denominator or historical health. Custody and every declared cleanup class are judged at current supported bounds. See [Portability and retention](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#portability-and-retention). **Acceptance.** 1. Populate product, authentication, rate-limit, drill, credential and attempt records; run expiry, maintenance and restart through runtime doors and compare surviving identities. 2. Only declared transient data/secret material disappears; no cleanup improves uptime or removes retained product history.

clauses.title: Operator-directed entity erasure
clauses.text: **Requirement.** An owner can erase a monitor with its evidence and dependent notification/heartbeat records, a destination with its credential copies, or an operator while another active owner remains. Monitor erasure requires typing the current monitor name. Each completed erasure returns a receipt with entity kind, per-table counts and completion time, and returns it only after the transaction containing the erasure, audit entry and portability fence succeeds. Requests based on stale monitor or destination state cannot re-create erased rows. The last active owner cannot be erased: local installations use `rer reset --yes`, while hosted installations require replacement by redeployment. Uptime has no R2 attachment feature; import-door uploads, plan snapshots and archive bytes are held in installation-local custody under the erasure rule in [Erasure and audit](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#erasure-and-audit). Already downloaded archives, messages already sent to external recipients and requests already in progress remain outside local erasure. See [Erasure and audit](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#erasure-and-audit). **Acceptance.** 1. Erase each supported entity through the owner API, including stale concurrent requests and the original owner with a successor. 2. Inspect the atomic per-table receipt, audit and journal; the last owner is protected and an old archive with the later journal cannot resurrect erased records.

clauses.title: Durable anonymized audit
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Destructive actions, automated notification attempts and operator authentication-mail sends also record the action, the subject kind and an opaque subject reference. Audit history is portable. The audit contains no monitor names, target URLs, email addresses or destination URLs. See [Erasure and audit](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#erasure-and-audit) and [Portability and retention](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#portability-and-retention). **Acceptance.** 1. Perform destructive actions, notification attempts and authentication-mail attempts through public doors, erase an actor and round-trip an archive; inspect durable opaque subjects and anonymized actors without planted names, addresses, URLs or secrets.

clauses.title: Contact separate from health
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Only accepted scoped claims and signed results refresh server-time contact, the 120-second freshness threshold never proves process liveness or target health, and restart, unavailable reads and archive omission preserve that distinction. See [Contact, interface and delivery](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance.** 1. Read Never seen, make accepted idle claims/results, age contact, reject foreign requests and restart. 2. Reads and health checks do not refresh contact; unavailable reads and restore cannot imply runner or target health.

clauses.title: Honest durable operator feedback
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Textual state/freshness/reasons, immutable history, labels, keyboard controls and responsive layout expose persisted evidence; failed reads show Unknown, action errors survive polling, busy reconciliation excludes controls and editing rejects assertion overrides. Accessibility is Base's one bar (BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001); the human screen-reader pass and the VPAT are register rows. See [Contact, interface and delivery](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance.** 1. Use the real owner console at 1440 and 390 with healthy, stale, failing and unavailable monitors; edit assertions, force read/action errors and polling, navigate by keyboard and inspect focus, text state, overflow, accessibility tree and axe results.

clauses.title: Authorized installation-wide destinations
clauses.text: **Requirement.** An owner may configure email, signed JSON webhook, or Slack incoming webhook destinations for all monitors in one installation; only scheduled incident transitions generate automatic notifications, and a test send cannot change monitor evidence or incident state. The hosted Worker submits email through the configured Base mail adapter and sends webhooks and Slack without a private runner; a private runner can also claim notification work. Webhook destinations also take WEBHOOK-001's configurable method, content type, custom headers and payload template. Destination credentials are installation-local and are not restored from archives. See [Contact, interface and delivery](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#contact-interface-and-delivery) and [Network and credentials](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance.** 1. Create/rotate/disable email, Slack and signed webhook destinations, cause scheduled failure/recovery and a test send through actual Worker/runner delivery doors; inspect one job per enabled destination, credentials, exact signing, escaping and unchanged health for tests.

clauses.title: Bounded notification acknowledgment
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Each event and destination without receiver-side deduplication (email, Slack incoming webhooks and the other channels DELIVERY-002 names), every test send and every drill gets one automatic send attempt. A RER relay 429 with Retry-After confirms non-acceptance and queues another submission after that delay. For those sends HTTP 500, connection loss, timeout, and unknown outcomes remain uncertain and are not automatically sent again; deduplicating destinations retry and every route can fall back to another contact under DELIVERY-002. Accepted means the configured provider or endpoint acknowledged the request; it does not mean a person received, read, or acted on it. See [Contact, interface and delivery](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance.** 1. At authorized provider edges return accepted, proven-unaccepted relay 429, HTTP 500, timeout and connection loss; restart during claims. 2. Only the proven-unaccepted case requeues automatically; uncertain started sends never replay and acceptance remains distinct from receipt.

clauses.title: Public landing and documentation
clauses.text: **Requirement.** At the app origin, `/` is the unauthenticated Lobby, `/docs` is public documentation, `/setup` is first-run setup, and the private operator console and editor are `/app` and `/app/monitor`; private documents require an owner session. The separate marketing site serves `https://run-uptime.com/` and `https://run-uptime.com/run`. The app Lobby at `/` and the marketing landing at the run-site `/` are distinct surfaces. **Acceptance.** 1. Open app-origin Lobby, docs and setup signed out, then sign in for /app and /app/monitor; separately read the marketing site and /run. 2. Their routes remain distinct and private documents reject unsigned access.

clauses.title: Monitoring ownership and honest delivery claims
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Uptime owns checks, evidence, routing, repeat reminders and monitoring reports. It feeds full paging and responder coordination to [Oncall](https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall), PagerDuty or Splunk On-Call, and public incidents, branded pages and subscriber updates to [Lamp](https://github.com/just-every/run-lamp) or Atlassian Statuspage. Teams, Discord, Telegram, SMS, voice and push are supported target channels under the clauses below. One network label is one vantage; provider acknowledgment never proves human receipt or response. Geographic placement, browser execution and accessibility require their own measured evidence. **Acceptance.** 1. Configure an alert and a sibling handoff, inspect acknowledged/received/responded as separate facts and simulate lost probes/providers; no duplicate network labels, acknowledgment or missing evidence becomes a delivery or availability guarantee.

clauses.title: Recipient-reported alert drills
clauses.text: **Requirement.** An owner can run an alert drill on one destination: the existing test event with drill wording, sent once through the same path with no automatic resend, plus a one-time confirmation link (random capability, stored only as a bound hash, single use, 24-hour expiry, one drill and one destination). Opening the link shows a page; only a same-origin POST confirms, and unknown, used, expired and foreign links answer 404 alike. The console keeps Submitted, Acknowledged (or Uncertain/Failed with its code) and Recipient confirmed as separate lines, and does not measure whether anyone acted. A confirmed drill is a report by the recipient that one message reached a person at one time. It is never evidence of monitoring, a delivery guarantee or a human response, and it changes no monitor evidence, state or incident. Proof belongs to the destination's current credential: a new address or URL or a rotated secret makes it Never proven, and drill history stays with the installation, so a restored destination is Never proven. See [Alert drills](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#alert-drills). **Acceptance.** 1. Drill email, Slack and signed webhook through the actual delivery runtime: GET/HEAD never confirm, same-origin POST confirms once, expired/replayed/foreign links refuse, 500 stays uncertain, rotation resets proof and archives/logs contain no capability or endpoint secret.

clauses.title: Required configuration diagnostics
clauses.text: **Requirement.** A shared configuration table validates required and conditional bindings for the Worker, scheduled entry point, local app, preview, setup, deployment and private runner before each begins work. Missing or malformed required values stop the entry point and name the variable without printing its value; a Worker configuration failure returns 503, including at `/health`. Hosted mode requires the selected Base mail provider and its sender configuration when outbound mail is enabled. An explicit `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` permits hosted operation without a sender or sending credentials, with owner sign-in through the deploying checkout’s guarded `rer signin`; email links, invitations and email alerts remain unavailable. With `MAIL_PROVIDER` set to `rer`, a missing `MAIL_API_KEY` or a value containing whitespace refuses health and native runner claims before admission or durable work; a valid replacement and restart restore health and authenticated idle claims against the same persistence without mail or target work. Supersedes `BASE-OPS-001`'s one-second health budget with the owner-approved three-second readiness response budget of 16 October 2026 (RL-2). See [Configuration diagnostics](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#configuration-diagnostics). **Acceptance.** 1. Start each runtime entry point with required and conditional bindings missing/malformed; diagnostics name bindings without values and health returns 503. 2. Restore settings and recover; exercise D1/ASSETS faults inside the owner-approved three-second readiness response budget. **Bounded evidence (qualification pending).** `tests/public-paths.mjs` invokes `tests/startup-rer-relay-url-support.mjs` proveRerRelayUrlStartup once against the actual emitted Worker and independently migrated persistent D1. With MAIL_PROVIDER set to rer and a valid synthetic MAIL_API_KEY, independently missing and malformed non-HTTPS MAIL_RELAY_URL settings refuse health and an otherwise-valid native runner claim with 503 naming only the binding. The request origin is independent of the relay setting; captured diagnostics and responses withhold planted values, the observed outbound edge receives no requests, and every durable table remains exact, including populated owner admission, public counters and retained claim custody. A corrected synthetic HTTPS relay and restart on the same persistence restore health 200 and an authenticated idle claim without mail or target work. This qualifies only those two conditional-binding refusals and their correction; the current partial judgment, other configuration, readiness faults and timing, console, hosted and provider qualification remain unchanged. **Bounded sender evidence (qualification pending).** `tests/public-paths.mjs` invokes `tests/startup-mail-sender-support.mjs` proveMailSenderStartup once against the emitted Worker and independently migrated persistent D1. With MAIL_PROVIDER set to rer, valid synthetic relay authority and unrelated settings valid, missing and malformed mandatory MAIL_FROM settings each refuse health and an otherwise-valid scoped runner claim with 503 naming MAIL_FROM. Native owner admission, signed runner enrollment and inert retained custody precede refusal. Independently constructed request authority, captured value-free diagnostics, a zero-request outbound observer and complete readable durable snapshots, including SQLite sequences, demonstrate refusal without work. Correcting the sender and restarting the same persistence restores health 200 and authenticated idle claim 200; a wrong runner key still returns 401. Recovery permits only the named request-admission counts and runner-contact fields, preserving authority, custody and every other durable row without mail or target work. This qualifies only these sender cases and their correction; STARTUP-001 remains partial with all other binding, readiness, timing, console, hosted and provider obligations unchanged.

clauses.title: Declared sessionless paths and rate limits
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Every sessionless route and emitted static path is declared in `seed.json` with its authentication rule and rate-limit class. D1 applies owner-tunable per-client limits in fixed 60-second windows and returns 429 with `Retry-After` after the class limit. A declaration does not bypass route-specific session, runner, heartbeat or development-key checks. Limit values are marked estimated and not load-tested. See [Public paths and rate limits](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#public-paths-and-rate-limits) and [Integrity and authority](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance.** 1. Enumerate declared sessionless paths against emitted routes, exceed configured public limits, inspect Retry-After, and remove counter storage; each route retains its own authentication checks and admission fails closed.

clauses.title: Supported isolated browser transactions
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Login, signup and checkout are supported monitored customer paths with explicit intended outcomes, immutable revisions, safe synthetic accounts and scheduled consensus. A constrained editor and isolated Playwright execution share the same evidence and authority rules. Every required outcome must pass; missing browser/credentials is Unknown. Per-run process/profile isolation, sanitized environment, network filtering, hard time/byte limits and credential-origin binding apply to all scripts. An effect beyond an explicitly authorized synthetic transaction needs the owner's exact effect grant (API-004). A changed-definition recovery is labeled and never presented as proof of the original outcome. Support qualification covers independently placed real-browser vantages and the complete login, signup and sandbox checkout outcomes. Reusable scripts and fixtures are required under FLOW-002, failure artifacts under FLOW-003, browser/device coverage under FLOW-004, and setup/teardown and effects grants under API-004; secret-bearing grants require ACCESS-003 second-factor step-up, and reports spanning migrated history require HISTORY-001 source segments. FLOW-001 is done only when its own acceptance and each of these dependent clauses are done. **Acceptance.** 1. Configure supported login, signup and sandbox checkout journeys, run independent real-browser vantages, break required outcomes and recover through signed results. 2. Wrong credentials, missing elements, server errors, slow pages, private redirects/subresources, extra origins and absent browsers have distinct retained outcomes; weakened definitions cannot silently clear the original incident.

nonGoals: Real provider or production target actions before explicit authority and verification
Public communication, people paging, and independent geographic monitoring
Fresh-account hosted operation and recipient acceptance remain unverified

data: Target hostname, path and query, method, request time and runner source address; configured headers and request body where the monitor has them

Other request classes keep their existing identification

Owner-held Basic, bearer or Digest credentials, generated JWT authorization and configured headers/body are sent only to the exact authorized target origin and monitor; a configured client TLS certificate and proof of key possession may be sent there, while its private key remains local. Credentials, custom headers, body and client certificate are permanently stripped on a cross-origin redirect

Owner-authorized OAuth token acquisition and refresh send a form-encoded HTTPS POST to the exact public token URL: client ID and secret through the declared Basic or form authentication mode, grant type, requested scopes and the refresh token when applicable. Public DNS answers are validated and pinned; token redirects and target TLS trust exceptions are refused. Acquired access and rotated refresh tokens remain in owner-only runner-local state, outside observations, logs and product archives
The target returns status and headers plus a bounded response body used for assertions; raw response bodies are not retained in observations
An external canary is a status-only GET: it sends no request credential, custom header or body and reads zero response-body bytes; validated public redirect hops may also be contacted

Failing HTTP response excerpts are redacted before storage in a separate owner-only snapshot table; default retention is 90 days, configurable from 1 to 365 days. Body text is escaped in the console; no screenshot or script execution is enabled. Canary response bodies remain unread.

clauseSummaries.text: Versioned monitor definition files and saved monitor pages are previewed without writes and validated with the editor’s rules. Applying a matching plan creates paused monitors or new revisions that preserve enablement, maintenance and runner assignments. Files carry no request secrets or installation authority and cannot enable monitors, issue heartbeat tokens or change notification destinations. Batch undo preserves history and reports revision conflicts. Imported history never becomes current evidence. No real third-party export or hosted import has been measured.

original.title: Reviewed definition files and inactive imports
original.text: **Requirement.** A versioned definition file (2 MiB, 500 monitors, UTF-8 JSON, editor fields only, no request secrets or installation authority) or saved UptimeRobot v3 monitor pages are previewed without writes as create, unchanged, change, refused or unsupported per entry with a plan digest, validated by the editor's own validation; apply refuses a digest that no longer matches and otherwise resumes the reviewed plan in bounded transactional batches as new paused monitors or new revisions that keep enabled, maintenance and runner assignments; nothing in a file enables a monitor, issues a heartbeat token, schedules a notification or touches a destination. Undo pauses what it created and restores what it changed while their revisions are unchanged, reports the rest and never removes history. Legacy definition batches travel in archives as restored history without authority; import-door custody stays installation-local. Through this definition-file door a log export is recognized and counted only. Storing it as labeled source history for reports is HISTORY-001's migration import, and no imported history ever becomes evidence. See [Definition files and imports](docs/contract/safety-rules.md#definition-files-and-imports). **Acceptance.** 1. Preview, apply, export and undo definition JSON and saved UptimeRobot pages through the owner routes and CLI. 2. Malformed/hostile/secret-bearing inputs and stale digests write nothing; creations stay paused, changes keep operational state, unsupported fields are named and history is never made current evidence.

clauses.title: Event identity and alerts
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Persist accepted events separately from alerts and human incidents. Identity is source plus eventId; conflicts compare the normalized allowlisted signal fields (canonical timestamps and trimmed strings), rather than irrelevant JSON whitespace or order or discarded fields. Repeated source event IDs return the original receipt; changed bytes with the same identity conflict. Receipts, admission order, the decision snapshot and the alert change commit atomically. Each signed or bearer source is explicitly scoped to service identities, and the service binds its environment. A deduplication key groups active alerts only within its source, service and environment; on the native Events API lifecycle generation is required, and trigger and recovery must carry the same generation. Recovery before trigger creates a recovered tombstone; a later trigger for that generation records evidence without reopening, reopening needs a new generation, and a delayed recovery can only close its own generation, never a new alert. Recovery affects the matching alert and never resolves an incident. **Acceptance.** Through the signed and bearer native intake doors: 1. Signed and bearer events are accepted; repeating a normalized identity returns the original receipt, changed content under the same identity conflicts, a recovery sent before its trigger stays recovered, a recovery sent after a newer generation leaves the newer alert unchanged, and protected state shows each result. 2. Grouping across multiple sources never merges service or environment boundaries.

clauses.title: Routing replay
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Retain the routing policy version and explanation at admission. Release 1 routes coordination ownership, with no timed escalation or paging. Replay is read-only: it returns the historical decision, ownership, policy and evaluation snapshot beside the proposed current decision, in submitted order, and produces no alert, incident or external effect; it does not claim schedule replay. Unmatched signals remain visible and unowned; suppression reasons remain inspectable. **Acceptance.** 1. Admit a severity-routed event, change the policy and replay it: the immutable admission explanation is compared with the proposed decision in submitted order, and durable state is unchanged before and after (zero writes).

clauses.title: Roles and authority
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Incident changes require an active authorized human session or an explicitly scoped OC-053 service-account capability (RL-2). A machine is attributed as a service account and never gains human-session, member-management or human-review authority. Viewer reads; responder coordinates; admin manages services, policies, members and import. All active members see all workspace incident data, and admin, responder and viewer permissions are separate from incident-commander attribution. Ingest credentials grant no read or human authority. Bearer and signed intake return only `duplicate`, the stored event `id`, the source `eventId`, `service`, `observedAt` and `acceptedAt` (201 accepted; 200 deduplicated). Routing decisions, snapshots and alert identities stay behind authorized read and export doors; scoped OC-053 reads disclose only granted service records, and archive and export authority remains session-protected. The status-only stakeholder role, with no incident, alert, runbook or archive access, is specified and tracked in OC-061. **Acceptance.** 1. Anonymous, expired, revoked, viewer, responder and admin sessions each get their role's outcome on reads, commands, sources and archives, and a real HTTP mutation held open while its author is revoked or downgraded publishes nothing. 2. Minimal intake receipts disclose no private routing data.

clauses.title: Incident state transitions
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Incident state transitions are explicit. Acknowledgment assigns responsibility. Resolution requires recovery evidence and a summary, independently of alert recovery. Optimistic revision checks reject stale edits. All accepted changes append an attributed timeline transactionally with state. Any active responder or admin can attest recovery and follow-up evidence; attestation is a human claim, not automatic measurement verification. This resolution rule governs declared incidents; an alert-only page that its source recovers closes without a human summary under OC-056. **Acceptance.** 1. Declare from admitted alerts and acknowledge; stale and concurrent changes are rejected; the source alert clears; resolution without evidence and a summary is refused; the incident then resolves, and its attributed timeline reads back over HTTP.

clauses.title: Copied runbooks
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Runbooks are copied into the incident at declaration; future service edits never silently rewrite incident instructions. Follow-ups carry owner, due date, open or completed state and completion evidence. Resolved incidents retain open work and editable review. **Acceptance.** 1. Declare an incident and edit its service runbook, and the copied incident steps remain unchanged; an owned, due-dated action requires completion evidence; unfinished work and the review are retained after resolution.

clauses.title: Bounded outbound incident effects
clauses.text: **Requirement.** In release 1, only signed OC-053 response events to an endpoint a current administrator explicitly approved may leave the incident workspace (RL-2). No paging provider notification, AI call, production action or Lamp publication occurs in release 1. Configured remote mail sends sign-in links only. Handoffs are minimum summaries with stable identity and visibility; an exported draft is explicitly unreviewed. Source links grant no access. External acceptance, delivery and acknowledgment are distinct later records. Approved OC-053 events are proved under OC-053. **Acceptance.** On a normal installation with no approved OC-053 endpoint: 1. Coordination and handoff preparation and export create no paging receipt, production action, AI call or external publication. 2. Draft exports remain unreviewed, and source links confer no access.

clauses.title: Native archive
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The native archive preserves services, policies, incident, alert, event and timeline identity and attribution, runbook and follow-up history. Archive and restore require current admin authority, and handoffs remain internal. Schema and references are validated before an atomic restore, and an invalid restore preserves existing data. Restore replaces application state while preserving the current administrator identity; credentials remain installation-local, other sessions are revoked, clients reload state, and historical and inactive identities are retained. Authentication secrets and sessions are never exported. Released migrations remain immutable. The full future paging archive is OC-052. **Acceptance.** Through the protected native archive door: 1. Export the archive, restore valid held records, and reject malformed references and storage failures without losing prior data. 2. Event, incident, runbook, action, timeline and attribution identity survive, and authentication material is absent from the archive.

clauses.title: User-authored records kept
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Authored incident records are kept through restart and export. Ingress accepts bounded structured fields. Provider and incumbent-compatible intake retain bounded structured evidence and no raw bodies under OC-059. Native Events API parsing is bounded to 64 KiB; authenticated oversized, malformed or incomplete native input retains only its first 64 KiB or fewer of exact raw bytes as untrusted incomplete custody under OC-059, never parsed or routed from that prefix. Incumbent-compatible endpoints and provider adapters use the larger per-provider bounds of OC-059. There is no arbitrary remote fetching or runbook execution. Complete retention controls are OC-040. **Acceptance.** 1. Over-limit and malformed intake is neither parsed nor retained beyond its bound, and over-limit command input is refused. 2. Hostile structured text and runbook links display literally, with no script execution and no fetch. 3. Authored history is preserved after restart and export.

clauses.title: Accessible interface
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Apply BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001 to Oncall's web journeys and the native apps in OC-029. A failed write is visible and never shown as saved. An unavailable UI is never described as a pager coverage failure, because release 1 supplies no pager. Each release publishes a conformance report (VPAT 2.5 Accessibility Conformance Report, WCAG 2.2 edition) stating the result per success criterion and per surface; an unsupported criterion is named, never omitted (R-4). Named assistive-technology passes cover VoiceOver with Safari on macOS and NVDA with Chrome on Windows for web, and VoiceOver on iOS and TalkBack on Android for the apps; each completes sign-in, finding an incident in the filtered list (OC-060), acknowledge, snooze, reassign, schedule view and override (R-3). **Acceptance.** 1. Run declaration, acknowledgment, notes, schedules, overrides and preview against BASE-ACCESSIBILITY-001. 2. A real stale-write failure is announced with no saved claim.

clauses.title: Health and honest commands
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Health identifies the deployed version, operating commands describe actual local and hosted effects, and acceptance records distinguish local evidence from remote, provider and pilot outcomes. Capacity promises require measured evidence. Pager, timer, mobile and standby health are OC-026 to OC-029's, and paging measurements are OC-064's. Each new execution class proves its own durable failure diagnostics under door rule D-1 before it ships. **Acceptance.** 1. check and describe run with storage available and unavailable, health reports both states, and the deployed identity matches the actual build. 2. Local, hosted, provider and human-drill outcomes are recorded separately.

clauses.title: Calendar-day rotations
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Named-zone calendar-day rotations retain fixed primary and backup member slots. Hand-offs use the wall minute plus integer civil days, not fixed elapsed seconds. Repeated minutes explicitly choose earlier, later or reject; nonexistent or rejected boundaries produce visible gaps. Override intervals include their start and exclude their end; an overlap in the same role is rejected. Inactive, viewer and missing members do not shift slots. A duplicated primary and backup assignment leaves the backup unavailable. **Acceptance.** 1. Save primary and backup schedules and query the HTTP preview across spring and fall DST, ambiguous and nonexistent minutes, override edges and an overlap refusal; inactive, viewer and missing slots are retained as gaps, and duplicate primary and backup responders are detected.

clauses.title: Paging off
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Production paging is OFF, and the existing pager is authoritative (RL-1). Every normal-installation delivery attempt refuses with an explanation that an independent standby and a real-phone drill are required. No production paging provider sends, synthetic delivery proof, cron delivery, SMS, voice or push are performed. Escalation policies are inspectable configuration data, not active timers. A labeled demo simulation is not production delivery or acceptance. Native cutover additionally requires OC-026 to OC-029 and OC-038 real-phone and provider-failure acceptance. **Acceptance.** 1. On a normal installation, each delivery, job, tick, callback and resume door returns the paging-OFF refusal and creates no receipt. 2. Demo simulations are treated as simulations.

clauses.title: Held history stays historical
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Held synthetic job, receipt and callback identities remain historical data. Restore pauses pending jobs. Historical acknowledgment and explicit cancellation retain attribution; resume and new timer starts refuse while paging is OFF. An acknowledgment never proves recovery. **Acceptance.** 1. Restore held synthetic jobs, receipts and callbacks: pending work is paused, acknowledgment and cancellation keep their attribution, resume is refused, and incident recovery remains unchanged.

clauses.title: Side-effect-free previews
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Schedule preview, now/next and replay are side-effect-free; actual historical delivery claims remain labeled synthetic. Nothing in this release certifies production delivery. **Acceptance.** 1. Read now/next and the schedule and routing previews: durable state and receipt counts are unchanged, no timers or provider actions are created, and historical synthetic data stays labeled.

clauses.title: Strict module archives
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Strict module archive validation and atomic replacement remain supported. Imported pending historical jobs pause. Scope and local capacity limits remain explicit. **Acceptance.** 1. Round-trip the strict module archive through protected HTTP; unknown fields, broken references and an injected SQL failure are rejected atomically, callbacks are retained and pending historical jobs pause.

clauses.title: Recovery checkpoint
clauses.text: **Requirement.** A paired recovery checkpoint captures coordination and scheduling records with both revisions in one consistent storage snapshot, excludes authentication, and validates its envelope and intrinsic record integrity. Explicit current-admin restore replaces both datasets atomically, pauses imported pending jobs, preserves the current-password mapping rule and revokes prior authority exactly as coordination restore does. Missing references in retained paused or finished history remain evidence, never dispatch authority; missing references for pending jobs are invalid. Invalid input, capacity failures, storage failure or losing concurrent writes preserve the previous complete state and cannot revoke a winning restore's new session. Proof runs through the actual emitted Worker and D1 and the private local CLI. **Acceptance.** 1. The checkpoint door and the private CLI each capture and restore both revisions. 2. Malformed, capacity and storage failures and competing writes preserve the previous complete state, identity mapping is explicit, orphan history stays evidence, and earlier sessions are revoked without revoking the winning restore session.

clauses.title: Reviewed handoffs
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Persist explicitly authored, unsent handoff copy with an explicit intended audience, immutable incident and service snapshots and canonical content hashes. Preparation and review actions have stable identities that conflict on changed content. Only current active responders and admins prepare, review or withdraw; viewers inspect permitted internal records and admins restore. A review binds exact copy and source versions, becomes ineligible on source drift or a recovery hold, and never grants sending, publication, recovery verification or independent-review authority. Withdrawal is terminal and preserves attributed append-only history. OC-006 and historical unreviewed envelopes stay unchanged. Separate additive handoff storage and archive are bounded to 64 records, 128 history entries per record, 128 KiB per record and 1 MiB aggregate. Explicit checkpoint version 2 includes handoffs; version 1 remains supported. Restore retains historical identities and holds active approvals atomically alongside existing recovery and credential and session safeguards. Invalid input, capacity or storage failure or losing concurrent writes preserve the complete prior state. HANDOFF-STAGE.md defines retained snapshots, eligibility and permissions. No provider send, remote fetch or Lamp publication is authorized. **Acceptance.** 1. Prepare, review, inspect and export exact handoff copy over protected HTTP; change the source or revision, withdraw, restore versions 1 and 2 and race writes. 2. Eligibility and holds, stable action identities, append-only attribution and every storage bound hold, with no send authority.

clauses.title: Maintained root commands
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Maintained root seed commands use the pinned Base installer, owner identity, dev identity and theme, with the published rer version that package.json pins and the effects OPERATIONS.json declares. Ordinary email-link sign-in is kept and tested independently of dev identity. Setup creates no example incident or service. Release 1 supports hosted coordination beside the existing pager without an independent standby (RL-1); portable SQL batch bindings are required. `rer deploy` verifies deployment identity, claims the configured owner automatically and retires the setup token. Hosted email-link sign-in requires a configured remote mail provider. Removal with the same Cloudflare credentials deletes only recorded deployment resources and verifies that they are gone. On local and hosted apps, the configured owner uses native email links, while admin-created team members use installation-local workspace names and passwords; no invitations are sent. Local dev identity never grants hosted access, local dev and preview bind loopback, and anonymous first-admin bootstrap remains loopback-only. The hosted journey on a real Cloudflare account is field proof R-1. **Acceptance.** 1. The documented setup, dev, build, preview, reset, archive and deploy dry-run commands run, owner entry opens the workspace, and an admin-created member signs in by password.

clauses.title: Additive upgrade
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The additive upgrade removes the one-row coordination store after migrating every entity and original array order to relational tables. Released migrations stay unchanged. Held passwords and identities are preserved. New Base identity cannot silently claim held coordination data. **Acceptance.** 1. Seed the held one-row SQL data and migrate: the held password signs in, and every entity, nested history and original ordering compares equal through HTTP; a repeated migration and restart silently reassign nothing to Base identity.

clauses.title: Now/next and calendar feed
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Now/next explains current coverage and each role's next effective hand-off. The private ICS feed uses the same resolved UTC boundaries, including overrides and gaps, and exports primary and backup separately. It requires a current session; the default window is seven days, and explicit windows are bounded to 31 elapsed days. Calendar downloads carry no public bearer access. Alert intake records immutable events with scoped source credentials; intake never starts paging. **Acceptance.** 1. Read now/next and the authenticated ICS feed for the seven-day default and bounded explicit windows: primary and backup UTC boundaries, overrides and gaps are correct, unauthenticated access is denied, and admission starts no paging.

clauses.title: Move-in preview
clauses.text: Saved export files enter a reviewed move-in preview with zero native-object writes. A current administrator reviews the exact source fingerprint before applying; people and services must be explicitly mapped, and schedules and policy data stay paused. Original files, rejected objects, unmapped fields, the journal and provenance remain available. Missing detail exports reject, and unmappable rotations or rules are named without approximation. The flow grants no login rights, activates no routing credentials and calls no source account or API. Complete migration and real-export acceptance remain separate requirements. The Site has no verified real-data importer receipt for named products.

clauses.title: Resume and undo
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Journaled imports support bounded resume after restart and explicit undo. SQL checks current actor, session and admin authority inside publication and reversal. Changed source identities require a reviewed catch-up through the shared door; outside that lifecycle they conflict. Duplicate unchanged sources are idempotent. Undo removes only unchanged attributed native objects; edits are preserved with an explicit conflict. Invalid input or failed publication leaves prior committed state unchanged; partial progress remains visible and resumable. **Native proof.** In `tests/activation.mjs`, the per-vendor “unfinished checkpoint” journey applies one bounded batch of a PagerDuty or Opsgenie saved file, proves its checkpoint is strictly inside the reviewed total, restarts the Worker, and completes the same job and fingerprint. It compares the committed prefix unchanged, checks each remaining object exists once, retries the completed job without new effects, and undoes exactly that import while native membership and paging state remain unchanged. The injected native SQL failure and expired publication lease legs distinguish rolled-back publication from retained partial effects that require explicit rollback. The same file's saved-response journeys cover unchanged replay, and its native-edit and later-import journeys preserve records under `NATIVE_EDIT_CONFLICT` and `IMPORT_SUPERSEDED`, including revoked-session refusal. In `tests/import-door.mjs`, the PagerDuty account HTTP journey revokes Business import authority inside the committing batch, injects publication failure, and checks unchanged native records; its identical-byte and reviewed catch-up journeys cover unchanged and changed identities. These are synthetic saved-file proofs with imported objects inactive and paging OFF; live account conversion and cutover remain with OC-038 and OC-074. **Acceptance.** 1. Apply, interrupt and restart, resume and undo both vendor imports over HTTP; revoke authority at publication, inject an SQL failure, replay unchanged and changed identities, and preserve native edits as named undo conflicts.

Runtime checks and review evidence are recorded separately; source metadata does not establish hosted, provider or npm publication acceptance.

clauses.title: Bounded admission
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Native version-1 JavaScript, Python and Go exception envelopes require active exact-project ingest credentials, registered release/build identity and bounded fields. Invalid, oversized, volume-limited and conflicting retries have explicit outcomes. Each project admits at most 120 outcomes a minute (`minute_budget`) and retains at most 10,000 events (`retained_event_budget`); over-limit intake returns 429 with `Retry-After` and a counted outcome. GOV-003 carries the target that replaces both limits with its named volume reasons and published sustained rate. Artifact URLs in envelopes are never fetched. Sentry error intake follows SDK-009's default acceptance with no release or an automatically created release/dist; only SDK-028's opt-in registered-sequence-only policy requires registration. Native version-1 intake keeps the registered release/build prerequisite. The broader SDK target is SDK-001, and runtime SDK compatibility is SDK-001 and SDK-012 to SDK-019. **Acceptance.** Through public ingest: 1. A valid native envelope is accepted, with its outcome. 2. Invalid, oversize, foreign-project and conflicting-retry envelopes each get their explicit refusal outcome, and the stored rows are unchanged. 3. Exceeding the per-minute limit returns 429 with `Retry-After` and a counted reason, with no partial rows. 4. Exceeding the retained-event limit returns 429 with `Retry-After` and a counted reason, with no partial rows.

clauses.title: Atomic acceptance
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Accepted means a sanitized occurrence, its group aggregate and its local new/regression alert commit atomically. Retry identity is project plus event ID and SHA-256 of canonical original accepted JSON before scrubbing: identical retry never increments, changed raw content conflicts even if its sanitized result matches. Raw bytes are not retained. Group algorithm version and basis remain inspectable. **Acceptance.** Through public ingest: 1. An event ingested twice yields one occurrence and one aggregate increment. 2. It raises one local alert. 3. The same event ID with a changed raw secret is an explicit conflict, with no partial rows.

clauses.title: Scrub before storage
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Apply the native allowlist, bounded text, query/fragment removal and sensitive-text scrubbing before persistence. Native envelopes contain no headers, cookies, request bodies or personal user identity; the `user` interface that unmodified Sentry SDKs send is governed by SDK-008's project identity policy instead. An optional random installation identifier supports bounded exposure measurement; it is never a name or address. Telemetry, source and notes are untrusted data and cannot authorize execution. The event fields SDK-010 keeps from unmodified Sentry SDKs (frame local variables, SDK-sent source context lines, exception values, tags, contexts, request, extra and thread stacks) pass through these scrubbers and SDK-003's server-side rules before storage, and default secret names are masked inside frame variables. Default protection persists when SDK-003 and CTX-002 introduce opt-in context; those captures require their own field policies and previews. Redaction does not promise removal of arbitrary semantic personal data. **Acceptance.** Privacy canaries ingested through public ingest: 1. are absent from stored events; 2. are absent from issue views; 3. are absent from evidence packets; 4. are absent from archives; 5. are absent from alert delivery content; 6. while the ordinary diagnostic content beside them survives.

clauses.title: Separated authority
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Every private API/document checks the current owner session or its exact ingest, deploy or read-only project grant itself. Cookie writes enforce same origin. Revocation and identity fencing take effect on the next request; confidential maps are never public. Ingest cannot read, deploy can only register releases/upload artifacts and record deployment starts/callbacks, and read-only agent grants cannot mutate. TEAM-001 extends this model to collaborative membership without broadening existing credentials. **Acceptance.** Each private transport: 1. refuses an anonymous call; 2. refuses a wrong-scope grant; 3. refuses a foreign-project grant; 4. refuses a revoked grant on the next request; 5. refuses an identity-fenced grant; 6. leaves state unchanged after every denied write; 7. and a direct map URL reveals no private bytes.

clauses.title: Source map identity
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Private flat Source Map V3 lookup matches project, release, build, debug ID and SHA-256 before presenting original coordinates. Missing, invalid or mismatched maps retain generated frames and a reason. Late uploads never rewrite immutable admission snapshots; current lookup is labeled separately. Lines are one-based, columns zero-based. SRC-004 carries indexed maps, `sourceRoot`, published capacity and opt-in source fetching; outside that opt-in, Spool never fetches a remote URL. SDK-010 rich stacks retain up to 1,000 frames per exception; SRC-004 and this clause inherit expanded mapped lookup without discarding retained SDK stack evidence. Broader artifact processing is SRC-001 and SDK-002. **Acceptance.** A minified exception from a second origin: 1. captured before its matching map is uploaded keeps generated frames with a reason; 2. captured after the upload shows its original coordinates; 3. keeps its earlier admission diagnostics unchanged after the late upload, with current lookup labelled separately; 4. keeps generated frames with a reason when the uploaded map does not match; 5. and its evidence packet excludes the confidential source.

clauses.title: Audited triage and regression
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Revision-checked open, acknowledged, resolved and suppressed changes are audited. An issue resolved in its current release reopens as a regression on a recurrence in a later release; delayed older-release events cannot invent one. For native version-1 events the order is the registered sequence, never guessed semver; Sentry events follow the project's stated rule in SDK-028, including releases later enriched by registration. SDK-009 carries resolve in the next or a named release and plain Resolve, and plain Resolve regresses on the next accepted event in any release; TEAM-004 inherits resolution from a commit's release, and TEAM-003 carries same-release recurrence policies, bulk actions and collaborative triage. Recognized JavaScript bundle hash suffixes do not split grouping; native anchors and reported frames stay immutable. Corrections retain exact occurrence provenance and reversible fenced apply/undo. **Acceptance.** 1. A captured issue resolved in its current release reopens as a regression when its fingerprint arrives in a newer release. 2. A later event from an older release does not reopen it. 3. Split and merge previews through the owner HTTP door and the issue view move nothing. 4. Split and merge apply and undo through the owner HTTP door and the issue view. 5. A stale revision is refused. 6. Original membership stays inspectable after apply and undo.

clauses.title: Sanitized evidence packet
clauses.text: **Requirement.** A compatible v1 packet exposes issue/lifecycle/grouping, retained release sequence and per-event release/build/environment, generated/original coordinates, immutable diagnostics beside current lookup, links and coded coverage gaps. UTF-8 JSON is bounded to 256 KiB and ten events, removing oldest events first and naming included/available counts even if none fit. It excludes source snippets, sourcesContent and artifact bytes. It carries the latest computed repair observation and newest three owner-recorded repairs, with omitted history named. CLI and stdio MCP keep exact-project read authority and untrusted/no-execution labels; they cause no model egress. **Acceptance.** 1. The same packet reads through HTTP, the CLI and the official MCP transport, with equal projections. 2. At the size boundary the oldest events are removed first and the included and available counts are named. 3. At the retention, import and loss boundaries the packet carries each coded coverage gap. 4. The packet carries no secrets. 5. It carries no source bytes. 6. Reading it performs no write. 7. A cross-project read is refused.

clauses.title: Loss counters and repair observation
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Expose windowed accepted/rejected/budget outcomes, SDK-reported discards by category and reason, and unknown pre-transport loss. Reported discarded errors are a loss input and prevent a quiet feed from proving a repair; other discarded categories do not imply lost errors. Only the owner records revision-checked repair links, scrubbed notes, checks, approval/merge/deploy facts and an exercised-flow record. Links are HTTPS origin/path text and never fetched. Manual repair writes send no notifications or external work. Compute recur/reasoned inconclusive/no-recurrence-after-exercise from stored release sequence, maps, events, exercise and loss; list older-release events separately. Missing exercise, capture, map, exposure or retention yields inconclusive. Never label a quiet feed fixed. Repair recurrence counts retained native admission membership, current membership and exact occurrence membership during the repair's lifetime, even after further corrections or undo; any applied or undone correction involving the issue leaves a `grouping_changed` coverage gap, so without retained recurrence its observation is inconclusive. AI-004 adds rate-based live proof. **Acceptance.** 1. The owner records a repair through the HTTP door. 2. Every project-grant write to repairs is denied, with the rows unchanged. 3. A deployed repair with no events reads inconclusive, with a named reason. 4. A healthy exercised window reads no recurrence after exercise. 5. An older-release event is listed separately and does not count as recurrence. 6. A loss case reads inconclusive. 7. A recurrence reads recurred. 8. Manual repair records send no notification and start no external work.

clauses.title: Archive, restore and retention
clauses.text: **Requirement.** Versioned private archives carry stored source bytes, checksums, migration identity, triage, maps, repairs/checks, operator corrections and inert agent grouping proposals (including server-computed review snapshots), reproduction/fix/exposure history, sanitized Sentry evidence, feedback, capture/grouping/release policies and erasure journal. HTTP/CLI and legacy v1/v2 decoding share semantic validation. Source and maps are portable; run tokens, step leases, owner sessions, project grants, alert destination records/credentials and dispatch queues never travel; retained alert rules restore disabled and delivery history is historical. Restored schedules and quiet hours are disabled, restored snoozes and scheduled mail are historical and never send, and raw recipient receipts and passing-test authority do not travel. Older archives restore newly introduced collections empty under versioned rules. An archive holds at most 10,000 events per project and refuses more with `Archive event budget`; GOV-003 carries streaming archives of any retained volume, SRC-004 the artifact capacity and GOV-002 scheduled policies. Manual cutoff retention removes private derived content, keeps repair snapshots with coverage gaps and exposes the deduplication horizon. Imported history creates no active grant, dispatch or current repair proof. **Acceptance.** 1. A populated installation exports through the browser and through `rer`. 2. Each archive restores into an independent empty destination, and the retained records compare equal. 3. Restored work is inert: no active grant, dispatch or current repair proof. 4. A tampered archive is refused before any mutation. 5. A conflicting archive is refused before any mutation. 6. An import into a nonempty target is refused before any mutation. 7. After a manual retention cutoff, repair snapshots keep their coverage gaps.

clauses.title: Release gates
clauses.text: **Requirement.** A release must exercise real capture, symbolication, privacy, permissions, persistence and independent restore through the shipped app. Fresh setup has no demo rows. Private flows are accessible and responsive with explicit empty, failure and unavailable states. Source presence, local providers or a green build cannot substitute for hosted, mobile, integration or real-account acceptance; physical-device and buyer-account qualification are register rows. UX-001 and each connector clause specify the expanded product gates. **Acceptance.** 1. The named implemented journeys run on the emitted Worker. 2. Their end states are inspected at 1440 and 390. 3. Each supported runtime passes its qualification run (D-5) and each configured provider its sandbox or official-schema journey.

clauses.title: Base commands and native admission
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The public rer command contract uses declared Node/pnpm pins and one setup manifest for terminal/browser. Setup claims or preserves the owner and private settings, stops its temporary app and leaves empty product data; rer dev uses real assets/HMR and private local identity. Local dev grants never authorize deployed entry. Reset is confirmed/contained and preserves source, exports and deployment receipts. Deployment dry-run makes no provider request. Managed signed first-owner admission precedes auth dispatch; editor config independently checks the owner and has short expiry/exact-origin CSP. Actual owner-account deployment and provider acceptance are separate gates. **Acceptance.** In a fresh checkout and an independent destination: 1. Public `rer install`, `rer setup` and `rer dev` complete. 2. `rer export` and `rer import` move the installation into the independent destination. 3. `rer reset` completes. 4. The deployment dry run completes without a provider request. 5. Setup preserves an existing setup. 6. Setup rejects an unsafe answer path. 7. A reused managed claim is rejected. 8. Anonymous and project-grant editor access is denied.

clauses.title: Project and installation-owner erasure
clauses.text: **Requirement.** The owner erases one project, or their own personal data, with a count-only preview, a typed confirmation bound to the exact current plan, resumable destructive steps and a completion receipt with per-table counts and times and no personal values. Project erasure cascades from the project root through every declared store, withdraws a Sentry-imported project's import-kit custody and original export artifacts in the same batch, leaves portability tombstones and stale-write fences, runs one erasure at a time and never reuses an erased project's identifier; GOV-003 carries erasure within 15 minutes for 150,000 retained events. Owner self-erasure first transfers authority to a verified successor, so exactly one active owner remains; it refuses unsupported/ambiguous attribution, retained import custody and identifiers inside structural keys rather than damaging other people's data, and replaces only exact whole-token identifiers in captured data. Every owner write admitted before the handoff and completed after it is refused with `409 authority_changed`. Archives exported before an erasure are refused by the installation's restore fence, including archives holding only child rows, and by a fresh destination that first receives the post-erasure archive or a later journal. Team membership extends these permissions while keeping owner-only destructive confirmation and a verified authority successor. The preview and receipt name each retained scope exception and the external copies outside the local fence (docs/PROJECT-ERASURE.md, docs/OWNER-ERASURE.md). **Acceptance.** Through public setup, dev, HTTP, export and import: 1. Project erasure removes the canaries planted in every declared store. 2. The preview and the receipt carry counts and times only, with no personal values. 3. Wrong-scope, cross-origin and stale requests are refused and change nothing. 4. Owner self-erasure hands authority to a verified successor first, leaving exactly one active owner. 5. An interrupted erasure resumes to completion. 6. A pre-erasure archive is refused in the same installation and in a fresh destination that first received the post-erasure archive.
